answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph by bounded random walks, so a voter’s influence is spread only across vertices reachable within the walk limit. A sybil cluster whose links to honest vertices form a sparse external cut has low conductance; few walks cross that boundary, limiting the cluster’s aggregate voting weight. The fable of unrestricted endorsement fails here: even vertices named gale and yarrow cannot gain influence without sufficient cross-cut attestations.
